sessions.final_text:
`balances` and `settle` now print amounts with thousands separators, so `settle` on `examples/big.csv` shows `121,810.78` instead of `121810.78`.

`format_cents` in `tally/money.py` gained an opt-in `grouped` flag, and the two renderers in `tally/report.py` pass it. I did it that way because `export` also uses `format_cents`, and its CSV output stays ungrouped.

`checks/thousands.sh` passes, and the 19 unit tests pass. I also ran `settle` and `export` by hand to confirm the output. I recorded claims for all three criteria. I didn't add a unit test for the new flag or change the README.

- **balances**: holds (observed). The check passed on this tree, and `balances` on `examples/big.csv` prints `-121,810.78`.
- **spec**: holds (observed). `settle` also prints grouped amounts, e.g. `121,810.78`. `export` is the only other caller of `format_cents`, and it stays ungrouped. Only `tally/money.py` and `tally/report.py` changed.
- **regression**: holds (tested). All 19 unit tests pass.

The new `grouped` flag has no unit test of its own.

checks_run: interlock check run --criterion balances; interlock check run --criterion regression; python3 -m tally settle examples/big.csv; python3 -m tally export examples/big.csv | head -3; grep -n "balances\|settle" README.md | head

interlock claim add --criterion balances --strength observed --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion balances" --note "check passes on this tree"

interlock claim add --criterion spec --strength observed --tree auto --ref "python3 -m tally settle examples/big.csv; tally export" --note "settle prints 121,810.78; export CSV still ungrouped"
